techStack: Express 5.2.1, Zod 4.4.3, bcryptjs 3.0.3, better-sqlite3 12.11.1, jsonwebtoken 9.0.3, TypeScript ~6.0.2
Vitest 4.1.5 + supertest for testing; test env sets JWT_SECRET='test-jwt-secret'
bcryptjs (not bcrypt): import default as bcryptjs; SALT_ROUNDS = 10; use .hash() and .compare() (async)
TypeScript strict mode: noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters; ESM modules (module: esnext, moduleResolution: bundler)
Rate limiter is vi.mock'd in tests — PATCH endpoint will not be rate-limited during test runs
Express type augmentation in src/types/express.d.ts: req.validated (from validate middleware), req.jwtUser (from requireJwt)
features: requireJwt middleware exists at src/middleware/requireJwt.ts — sets req.jwtUser = { userId, email, username }; already used on GET /api/auth/me
validate() middleware exists at src/middleware/validate.ts — applies Zod schema to { ...params, ...body } for non-GET, sets req.validated, returns 400 on failure
ConflictError (409) and ValidationError (400) already defined in src/errors/index.ts — reuse directly
authService.getById(id) returns UserResult { id, email, username, createdAt } (no password) — follow same pattern in userService
authController.me() already uses req.jwtUser!.userId — B1 is satisfied, no change needed
app.ts mounts authRoutes; uses global middleware: requestId, rateLimiter, cors, express.json()
No userRoutes, userController, userService, or userSchema exist yet — all four must be created
architecture: Layer order: app.ts mount → route file (middleware chain) → controller → service → db singleton
Zod schemas live in src/schemas/; passed to validate() middleware; validated data lands in req.validated
DB singleton: import db from '../db/client'; synchronous .prepare(sql).get(id) / .run(...args) / .all()
Errors are thrown (not returned); global errorHandler in src/middleware/errorHandler.ts converts AppError subclasses to { error, code, requestId } JSON
UserResult shape (authService pattern): { id, email, username, createdAt } — password column must be excluded from SELECT or omitted from returned object
req.jwtUser typed in src/types/express.d.ts — no modification needed; contains { userId: string, email: string, username: string }
Controllers use async functions with try/catch and next(err) to pass errors to errorHandler
edgeCases: Empty body {} must return 400 — Zod .refine must require at least one of: username, email, currentPassword, newPassword (unknown keys are stripped by Zod before refine runs)
Body with only unrecognised keys (e.g. { foo: 'bar' }) must also return 400 — Zod strips unknown keys leaving {}, then refine rejects it
newPassword without currentPassword must return 400 — second .refine in schema catches this before the service is reached
Wrong currentPassword must return 400 with EXACT message 'Current password is incorrect' — throw new ValidationError('Current password is incorrect') from service
Atomicity on conflict (B9): request with { username: 'new', email: taken_email } must leave BOTH fields unchanged — check ALL uniqueness BEFORE executing any UPDATE
Username conflict (B10) and email conflict (B9) both return 409 — throw new ConflictError(...)
Password must never appear in response — SELECT only id, email, username, created_at; map created_at → createdAt
bcrypt hash stored in DB must match /^\$2[aby]?\$/ — use bcryptjs.hash(newPassword, SALT_ROUNDS) with SALT_ROUNDS = 10
Users table columns: id TEXT PK, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, username TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, password TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL
Response shape for PATCH 200: { user: { id, email, username, createdAt } } — camelCase createdAt mapped from created_at column
GET /api/auth/me query params ?id=X&userId=X must be ignored — only req.jwtUser.userId determines identity (already correct in authController, no change needed)

tasks.requirement: B3 — PATCH /api/users/me with empty body or no recognised fields returns 400; B5 — newPassword without currentPassword returns 400
tasks.description: Create src/benchmark-backend/src/schemas/userSchema.ts with a Zod object schema containing four optional fields: username (string), email (string), currentPassword (string), newPassword (string). Add two .refine calls: (1) at least one of the four fields must be defined; (2) if newPassword is present then currentPassword must also be present.

tasks.requirement: B4 — username update returns 200 with user object; B6 — wrong currentPassword returns 400 'Current password is incorrect'; B7 — successful password change allows login with new password; B8 — new password stored as bcrypt hash; B9 — email conflict returns 409 with no partial writes; B10 — username conflict returns 409; B11 — password never in response
tasks.description: Create src/benchmark-backend/src/services/userService.ts with an updateUser(userId: string, payload) function. Steps in order: (1) if newPassword present, SELECT password FROM users WHERE id = userId and bcrypt.compare currentPassword against the stored hash — throw new ValidationError('Current password is incorrect') on mismatch; (2) if email is changing, SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ? AND id != userId — throw new ConflictError if a row is found; (3) if username is changing, SELECT id FROM users WHERE username = ? AND id != userId — throw new ConflictError if a row is found; (4) build SET clause dynamically for changed fields, hash newPassword with bcryptjs.hash(newPassword, SALT_ROUNDS) if present; (5) execute single UPDATE users SET ... WHERE id = userId; (6) SELECT id, email, username, created_at FROM users WHERE id = userId and return { id, email, username, createdAt }.

Wraps in try/catch with next(err).
